title: How the compiled Wasmtime cache retires its entries
description: The compiled cache `<home>/.semio/cache/wasmtime/<engine-config-hash>/<package-hash>.cwasm` is derivable (a miss recompiles) and must not grow without bound. At engine start, and then at most every `minimumIntervalSeconds` (the stamp file of the cache root records the last run), complete `.cwasm` files go when their last use (modification time; a cache hit refreshes it every `touchIntervalSeconds` at most) is older than `maximumAgeSeconds`, and then, least recently used first, until the complete files together fit `maximumBytes`. A complete file used within `minimumIdleSeconds` is never retired, whatever the cap says (it may be open, or just written); a `.scratch` staging file of a writer goes only after `scratchGraceSeconds` (writes are temp + rename, so a complete file is never half written). At most `maximumEntries` files are looked at per run; deletions are single `remove_file` calls, a refusal (a file still mapped on Windows) leaves the file for the next run.
